one_line: Results beat and bookings are record, but guidance is thin, prices fell in the last quarter, and peers are cutting forecasts. The fall is partly fair.

why_fell.reason: Fear that AI cuts the work and price of consulting
why_fell.evidence: Trade press ties the sell-off to AI disruption worries across the sector. Systems integration and app development are nearly half of sales.
Guidance is 3-6% growth in local currency, slightly below some estimates. First-quarter sales guided to $18.95-19.60 billion, up 2-6%.

why_fell.reason: Prices fell in the latest quarter
why_fell.evidence: Management said pricing was stable for the year but lower in many areas in the fourth quarter, and that AI lets it pass on more savings.
Infosys cut its year growth forecast to 1-2%. Cognizant trimmed its range. TCS said it saw deflation.

for_unfair.point: Fiscal 2026 sales were $74.2 billion, up 5% in local currency, beating the 3-4% guide. Fourth quarter grew 7%, above the top of guidance.
Bookings were $22.2 billion in the quarter (1.2 times sales) and $84.5 billion for the year. Managed services hit a record $12.8 billion.
Free cash flow was $11.6 billion, margin rose to 15.8% adjusted, and at least $9.5 billion goes back to shareholders in fiscal 2027.

for_fair.point: Full-year bookings grew only 3% in local currency, a slow pace for the year. Peers are weaker still, so the whole group is slowing.
Everest Group estimates AI has lifted price deflation in IT services from about 2% to 5%. TCS called it degrowth. Infosys cut its forecast to 1-2%.
Management said hiring will slow in fiscal 2027, partly due to AI. Guidance already assumes intense competition, leaving little cushion.

what_market_fears: AI lets clients buy the same work for less, so prices and sales shrink faster than new AI work fills the gap.
what_would_prove_it_wrong: Two quarters of falling sales with falling prices would show it is real. Steady 3-6% growth with stable margins would show the fear is overdone.
next_date_to_watch: Fiscal Q1 2027 results, expected December 2026. Watch sales against the $18.95 billion floor.

flag.note: Sales are still growing 7%, but prices fell in many areas in the latest quarter, an early sign of the flagged risk.

not_found: Headcount change for the year not found in a filing (about 814,000 at year-end). Search results on a June 2026 price near $128 conflict with the briefed $232 price and were not used. IBM Q3 2026 consulting figures and TCS October results not confirmed. No direct client-pricing evidence beyond management comments.
